page: Amazon Web Services d3en.2xlarge is a dense storage instance optimized for network and EBS performance. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor operating at 3.1 GHz, featuring 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading and a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. A key hardware characteristic is its massive local storage capacity, consisting of 55,920 GB of local HDD storage.

Benchmark data indicates that the d3en.2xlarge delivers average performance across several computational and memory tasks, though it exhibits weaknesses in raw processing power. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and gzip compression single-threaded benchmarks fall into the bottom 25%, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is similarly weak. However, the instance achieves average results in Geekbench single-core tests, Passmark CPU scores, and Redis SET operations, which reach 6.7 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only large block transfers measured at 51.86 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the d3en.2xlarge is its combination of massive storage capacity with relatively modest CPU performance. It is not designed for compute-intensive workloads or LLM inference, where it scores in the bottom 10% for medium-sized models. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers high storage density per resource unit, making it suitable for storage-heavy applications that do not require high-speed SSD IOPS. Appropriate workloads include data warehousing, log processing, large-scale data lakes, and distributed file systems where sequential disk throughput and high capacity are prioritized over raw compute power.
